deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page): Gauss looks for right spherical triangles (hypotenuse r, legs p, q, angles P opposite p and Q opposite q) in which every side and angle has rational sine and cosine. He reduces the problem to finding two pairs of integers (a,b), (a',b') with ab(a^2-b^2) = k m^2 and a'b'(a'^2-b'^2) = k m'^2. Equivalently, two Pythagorean triangles whose areas have the same squarefree part, i.e. the same congruent-number class. He then gives half-angle tangent formulas for r, p, q, 90-P and Q. Such a triangle yields a 'pentagramma mirificum' (Napier pentagon), a spherical pentagram all of whose 10 'diagonals' are 90 degrees.

THIS PAGE, 'Beispiel'. Take (a,b) = (6,1) and (a',b') = (5,2).
- a^2-b^2 = 35 and ab(a^2-b^2) = 6*35 = 210.
- a'^2-b'^2 = 21 and a'b'(a'^2-b'^2) = 10*21 = 210.
- Hence k = 210 and m = m' = 1.
- The marginal '2210' is 37^2 + 29^2 = 2*1105, the common denominator before reduction.

Inserting into the previous-page formulas:
- tan(r/2) = m(a'^2+b'^2)/(m'(a^2+b^2)) = 29/37, giving r/2 = 38 05 20.
- tan(p/2) = m'ab/(m a'b') = 6/10 = 3/5. The alternative form 21/35 agrees. This gives p/2 = 30 57 50.
- tan(q/2) = 2aba'b'/(k m m') = 120/210 = 4/7, giving q/2 = 29 44 41.
- tan((90-P)/2) = (ab'-ba')/(aa'+bb') = 7/32, giving 12 20 20.
- tan(Q/2) = (ab'+ba')/(aa'-bb') = 17/28, giving 31 15 50.

Doubling via sin x = 2t/(1+t^2) and cos x = (1-t^2)/(1+t^2):
- r = 76 10 40: sin 1073/1105, cos 264/1105, tan 1073/264.
- p = 61 55 40: sin 15/17, cos 8/17, tan 15/8.
- q = 59 29 22: sin 56/65, cos 33/65.
- P = 65 19 20: sin 975/1073, cos 448/1073 (since 1073 = 32^2 + 7^2).
- Q = 62 31 40: sin 952/1073, cos 495/1073 (since 1073 = 28^2 + 17^2).

I checked the triangle relations (my verification):
- cos r = cos p cos q.
- sin p = sin r sin P and sin q = sin r sin Q.
- tan q = tan r cos P and tan p = tan r cos Q.
- cos P = cos p sin Q and cos Q = cos q sin P.
- cos r = cot P cot Q.
All hold exactly.

RIGHT-HAND TABLE. For each prime N = 2 or N ≡ 1 (mod 4) up to 109, written as N = x^2 + y^2 with y < x, Gauss lists the angle arctan(y/x), i.e. the argument of the Gaussian prime x + yi:
- 2: 45 00 00
- 5: arctan(1/2) = 26 33 54
- 13: arctan(2/3) = 33 41 24
- 17: arctan(1/4) = 14 02 10.48
- 29: arctan(2/5)
- 37: arctan(1/6)
- 41: arctan(4/5)
- 53: arctan(2/7)
- 61: arctan(5/6)
- 73: arctan(3/8)
- 89: arctan(5/8)
- 97: arctan(4/9)
- 101: arctan(1/10)
- 109: arctan(3/10)
The small '5' under 13 is probably the norm of the first prime he composes with.

The half-angles above are sums and differences of these, by factoring in Z[i] (my reconstruction):
- Q/2 = arg(6+i) + arg(5+2i) = 9 27 44 + 21 48 05, since (6+i)(5+2i) = 28 + 17i.
- (90-P)/2 = 21 48 05 - 9 27 44, since (5+2i)(6-i) = 32 + 7i.
- r/2 = 45 - arg5 + arg13 - arg17, since (1+i)(2+i)(3-2i)(4+i) = 29 + 37i.
- p/2 = 45 - arg17, since (1+i)(4-i) = 5 + 3i.
- q/2 = 90 - arg5 - arg13, since (2+i)(3+2i) = 4 + 7i.
This is how the numerical angles were obtained.

'Consecutive Theile des Fünfecks'. The five consecutive parts of the pentagon are:
- alpha = r
- beta = 90 - p = 28 04 20: sin 8/17, cos 15/17, tan 8/15.
- gamma = P
- delta = Q
- epsilon = 90 - q = 30 30 38: sin 33/65, cos 56/65, tan 33/56.
The columns list sin, cos and tan of each part. I verified the pentagram (Napier/Gauss) relations cos alpha = cot gamma cot delta, and cyclically. Each holds exactly:
- cos alpha = 264/1105
- cos beta = 15/17
- cos gamma = 448/1073
- cos delta = 495/1073
- cos epsilon = 56/65
Equivalently sec alpha = tan gamma tan delta, which is the relation written on the next page. The next page also gives tan of half of each part: 29/37, 1/4, 25/39, 17/28, 3/11.

'Stereographische Coordinaten'. The five vertices alpha', ..., epsilon' of the spherical pentagram are placed as complex numbers on the stereographically projected sphere.
- alpha' = 0
- beta' = 17/28 (= tan(Q/2), on the real axis)
- gamma' = (1073 + 264i)/1105, on the unit circle, i.e. 90 degrees from alpha'
- delta' = i
- epsilon' = (-1320 + 5365i)/8619
I verified the five required orthogonalities (great-circle distance 90 degrees), using the criterion |1 + z conj(w)| = |z - w|:
- alpha'gamma' and alpha'delta' (both points on the unit circle).
- beta'delta'.
- gamma'epsilon': Re(epsilon' conj(gamma')) = (-1320*1073 + 5365*264)/(8619*1105) = 0.
- beta'epsilon': (1-b^2)(1-|z|^2) + 4b Re z = 0 with b = 17/28; exact.
Number-theoretically, 8619 = 3*13^2*17 and |epsilon'| = 5525/8619 with 5525 = 5^2*13*17.

The second column gives the antipodal configuration z -> -1/conj(z):
- infinity
- -28/17
- -gamma'
- -i
- (792 - 3219i)/2125
I checked: -1/conj(epsilon') = 8619(1320 - 5365i)/5525^2 = (792 - 3219i)/2125.

The last two columns are the same points multiplied by 20, apparently for drawing a figure of radius 20:
- beta': 12.1 and -32.9
- gamma': 19.4 + 4.8i and its negative
- delta': ±20i
- epsilon': -3.1 + 12.4i and 7.5 - 30.3i
The crossed-out entries had real and imaginary parts swapped and were corrected.
errors: No substantive errors: all rational sines, cosines and tangents, all triangle identities, all pentagram identities and all stereographic coordinates check exactly.

Minor second-level rounding in the sexagesimal angles. Half-angles are rounded to 10 arcseconds or truncated, and the doubled values inherit this. Exact values: r = 76°10'39.0", p = 61°55'39.0", q = 59°29'23.1" (written 59 29 22), P = 65°19'18.6" (written 65 19 20), Q = 62°31'38.9" (written 62 31 40), epsilon = 90 - q = 30°30'36.9" (written 30 30 38). arctan(4/7) = 29°44'41.6" is truncated to 41.

Self-corrected slips on the page: in epsilon' (both columns) the numerators of the real and imaginary parts were first interchanged (5365/1320, 3219/792), then corrected. The scaled values -12.4+3.1i and +30.3-7.5i were likewise struck and corrected to -3.1+12.4i and +7.5-30.3i. A struck tangent entry in the epsilon row was replaced by 33/56.

results.what: Explicit rational right spherical triangle (all sides and angles with rational sin/cos) generated from the pairs (6,1), (5,2), whose Pythagorean-triangle areas share squarefree class 210: r, p, q, P, Q with sin/cos 1073/1105, 264/1105; 15/17, 8/17; 56/65, 33/65; 975/1073, 448/1073; 952/1073, 495/1073
results.modern_name: Rational (Heronian-type) right spherical triangles; parametrisation via Pythagorean triples and congruent-number classes
results.usually_credited_to: Not a standard named result; rational spherical triangles were studied sporadically in the 19th–20th c. The congruent-number condition goes back to Fibonacci/Euler.

results.what: Pentagramma mirificum with all ten parts rational: consecutive parts alpha..epsilon with cos alpha = cot gamma cot delta cyclically; tan(1/2 part) = 29/37, 1/4, 25/39, 17/28, 3/11
results.usually_credited_to: Napier (rules), Gauss (pentagramma mirificum, Nachlass, Werke III)

results.what: Table of arguments arctan(y/x) of Gaussian primes x+yi for norms 2,5,13,...,109, used to compose angles additively via factorisation in Z[i]
results.modern_name: Arctangent / argument table of Gaussian primes (Machin-type decomposition)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (table of arctangents of Gaussian primes in his Nachlass, Werke II); Machin, Euler for arctan formulas

results.what: Stereographic complex coordinates of the five pentagram vertices, with 90° conditions verified via |1+z conj w| = |z-w|, and the antipodal map z -> -1/conj z
results.modern_name: Stereographic projection / Riemann-sphere chordal geometry in complex coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Stereographic projection is ancient; complex-coordinate use is associated with Gauss and Riemann

deep.surprise_reason: The pentagramma mirificum and Gauss's arctangent table for Gaussian primes are known parts of his Nachlass. What is less known is the explicit construction of a fully rational pentagram via pairs of Pythagorean triangles with areas in the same congruent-number class (k=210). Also less known is his placement of it in exact rational complex stereographic coordinates. This is a notable unpublished detail, not a major theorem.

checkable.asserts: Both pairs give ab(a^2-b^2)=k m^2 with k=210, m=m'=1
Half-angle tangents of r, p, q, 90-P, Q
cos r = cos p cos q
sin p = sin r sin P, sin q = sin r sin Q
cos r = cot P cot Q
Pentagram relations cos(part) = cot·cot of the two opposite parts, cyclically
Angle table: evaluate *180/pi to compare with 26°33'54", 33°41'24", 14°2'10.48", 16°41'57"
Gaussian-integer factorisations underlying the additive composition of the half-angles
